openings.claim: Tight downward hatch pressure may be unnecessary for lateral retention: removable strip stops could carry the sideways load while gentle distributed seating preserves the seal. This is a proposed counterexample, not a demonstrated joint.
openings.delta: Replace the hatch-pressure-to-friction dependency with hatch-edge-to-strip-to-rim bearing. Propose two opposed removable rim jaws, each using two supplied strips, bolts and rubber pads; their inner edges register the hatch. Cord tethers recover detached parts, which park outside the inspection opening. Rim attachment still requires adequate grip; the removal concerns tight pressure on the hatch.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: ordinary tighter clamping supplies enough friction to prevent sliding. If stops work, light seating should meet the 1 mm/20 N requirements without the opposite-corner lift associated with tighter left-corner pressure. If only tighter seating succeeds, the proposed removal fails. Neither this counterexample nor its failure establishes a converse or inverse necessity claim.
openings.probe: First check whether actual rim geometry permits padded jaws, positive edge bearing and complete exterior parking using only supplied tools and stock. If feasible, compare tighter friction seating with stop registration using the same stock sequentially. Give each configuration ten opening cycles and six closure/pull trials at cycles 1, 2, 4, 6, 9 and 10; place the supplied card at the right contact on final closure in each. Measure displacement, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal damage. Twelve pulls total. Defeat: slipping jaws, ineffective bearing, displacement over 1 mm, reopening over 30 seconds, tears, obstruction or fabrication/observation overruns. Stop if safe assembly cannot be achieved.
assumptions: Unprovided rim profile and access must permit jaw attachment and edge registration without modifying protected parts.
Strip stiffness, jaw grip, pad behavior and technician release speed are unknown; the time caps do not establish feasibility.

assessment: One uncertain removal candidate. Fabrication and probe only; no deployment or performance claim. All hard constraints and disturbed-closure outcome requirements remain acceptance conditions.
